hlaford.hook: From Old English hlāford, meaning "lord, master of servants or slaves".

chain.gloss: lord, master of servants or slaves

firstUse.quote: The King was considered as the hlaford of the nation; and in consequence of that supposition, the security given to inferior hlafords against their particular retainers was in his case extended to all
firstUse.source: 1830, John Allen, “Tardy Growth of Many of the Royal Prerogatives”, in Inquiry into the Rise and Growth of the Royal Prerogative in England, London: […] Longman
